description: CosmosReborn is a team of individuals interested in space missions, game design and innovative solutions to problems. For the Space Mission Design Game, we aim to create an entertaining and original game. We are looking for individuals interested in being innovative and hard working with skills in space related subjects, game design, UI/UX design, graphic design or programming.
summary:
Cosmos Reborn is a browser game about surviving and building on the Moon, made for the Space Mission Game Design challenge. After crash-landing, players salvage their ship, build a base, grow a settlement of survivors and build a rocket home across five story acts.
Real mission science drives the gameplay:
    •    Fuel comes from ice drilled in permanently shadowed craters and turned into propellant, as NASA plans for Artemis.
    •    The radio dish shows live NASA Earth rotation data.
An AI assistant gives voice hints, and up to four friends can play together. The game makes the challenges of a lunar mission personal, and fun to learn.
details:
How it works: players gather, craft and build, keep civilians fed, defend against raids, and assemble and fuel a rocket. A choice near the end decides between two endings. The MOONLINK AI gives hints, never answers, and you can talk to it by saying "Hey AI".

Impact: it teaches what really decides whether a lunar mission survives (water ice, fuel, food, power, shelter) through choices players make, not through text to read.

Tools:

    •    TypeScript, React, Vite and HTML Canvas, with a custom pixel-art engine;

    •    Node.js and WebSockets for multiplayer, hosted on Render;

    •    Gemini for the AI assistant and ElevenLabs for voices and speech recognition;

    •    NASA CDDIS Earth Rotation data.

Creativity: a mystery story told through logs and a glitching AI, with science as a game mechanic, plus cutscenes, voiced characters, creatures, boss fights and a space-battle ending.

What we considered: scientific accuracy, no install needed, clear step-by-step instructions, and keeping API keys secure. Playtester feedback shaped the instructions, popups and waypoints.
